nodes.description: Incomplete polypeptides are potentially toxic, and stalling additionally sequesters ribosomal subunits away from the translation-competent pool, so the consequence is both a proteotoxic burden and a drain on translational capacity. Neurons appear particularly exposed: NEMF is expressed more strongly in excitatory than inhibitory cortical neurons and most strongly in developing excitatory neurons. In Nemf-mutant mice the downstream cellular phenotype includes cytoplasmic mislocalisation and aggregation of proteins also implicated in adult neurodegeneration, alongside an Importin-beta-specific nuclear import block.

nodes.description: A CRISPR-derived frameshift allele producing no detectable full-length NEMF. More severe than either missense allele, with pre-weaning lethality by postnatal day 11, establishing that the missense alleles are hypomorphs.

A second ENU missense allele, in the coil motif that assists A-site tRNA recruitment. Milder and slower than R86S: abnormal gait and hindlimb wasting from ten weeks, with survival beyond two years, and continuing proximal axon loss between 8 and 55 weeks.

An ENU-derived homozygous missense allele in the NFACT-N domain, near the conserved catalytic residues required for C-terminal tailing. The most severe of the two missense models, with a waddling gait from two weeks and a median lifespan of 20 days.

Cultured mouse primary cortical neurons with Nemf knocked down, assayed by immunofluorescence for axon outgrowth and synapse formation. This is the only system in which the developmental arm of the mechanism has been measured directly.

nodes.description: NEMF performs two separable jobs on the obstructed 60S subunit. It stabilises LTN1/Listerin binding so the nascent chain is ubiquitylated, and it catalyses untemplated C-terminal tailing, which exposes ribosome-buried lysines to LTN1 and also creates a C-terminal degron read by CRL2-KLHDC10 and Pirh2 independently of Listerin. Disease-associated missense substitutions tested in the yeast ortholog selectively impair the tailing activity, and the severity of that biochemical defect tracks the severity of the corresponding mouse allele.
